previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, chronic pancreatitis, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for severe epigastric abdominal pain consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis. He presented with nausea, vomiting, and elevated lipase (226), but imaging showed no necrosis or complications. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control, with gradual advancement to a regular diet. He developed transient delirium likely due to opioid and antihistamine use, which resolved with medication adjustment. His hemoglobin dropped from 8.8 to 7.5 g/dL but stabilized without active bleeding signs. Pulmonary edema and pleural effusions were noted on imaging, attributed to heart failure, and his oxygen needs improved. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid combining hydroxyzine and diphenhydramine, monitor for GI bleeding, and follow up with his PCP for hemoglobin check at his next dialysis.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with h/o ESRD on HD, chronic pancreatitis, atrial 
fibrillation, and diabetes presenting with epigastric abdominal 
pain with hospital course complicated by fevers to 103.8, 
hypoglycemia, and diarrhea.  Pt. continues to do well off 
antibiotics and with volume removal by HD.

# Sepsis (resolved). On admission, pt. met SIRS criteria due to 
fever, tachycardia, and tachypnea.  No clear localizing source, 
however. Productive cough suggested pneumonia, though CXR was 
clear.  GI source also considered given abdominal distension. 
Pt. did briefly have diarrhea while on antibiotics, but c. diff 
was negative and it resolved once antibiotics stopped. No 
evidence of pancreatitis, despite hx chronic pancreatitis.  Pt. 
anuric. Blood cultures negative. Pt. was initially placed on 
broad spectrum antibiotics, but as no source was identified, 
these were discontinued.  He remained afebrile without 
leukocytosis or other symptoms. 

# Abdominal distension. Pt. admitted with significant abdominal 
distension on exam.  Ct abdomen/pelvis on admission was 
concerning for SBO. Pt., however, did not have abdominal pain, 
nausea, or vomiting and continued to pass gas and have bowel 
movements throughout.  His distension improved with a good bowel 
regimen and volume removal via hemodialysis. 

# Pulmonary edema. Pt. with new oxygen requirement during this 
admission of ___ via nasal cannula. Chest xray suggestive of 
volume overload and his symptoms improved with large volume 
removal at hemodialysis. 

# Hypercalcemia.  Unclear etiology. ___ be secondary or tertiary 
hyperparathyroidism related to CKD. Could also be related to 
activated vitamin D or underlying malignancy. Elevated PTH. 
Renal will continue to monitor and will further evaluate as 
outpatient.

# Hypoglycemia/DM. Last HbA1c 10.7 on ___. Pt with multiple 
complications including peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, 
nephropathy. Pt. with significant hypoglycemia on admission 
likely due to insulin administered either by the pt at home or 
in the ED during treatment for hyperkalemia. Pt. was back on 
home insulin regimen by discharge.

# Afib with RVR. Pt. initially in RVR on admission, but 
successfully controlled with IV and PO diltiazem. Pt. not on 
anticoagulation due to history of GI bleeds. Pt. not on BB as 
active cocaine user. Pt. was continued on home diltiazem and 
digoxin.

# Anemia. Pt. with known history of chronic GI bleeds from 
colonic ulcers, severe esophagitis, gastritis, and 
angioectasias. Per OMR, needs inpatient ___ and capsule 
endoscopy.  GI notified but would like to defer to future 
admission given concern for SBO. During this admission, stools 
were non-bloody, and there was no evidence of acute GI bleed. 
There was no evidence of hemolysis on labs. Iron was low, though 
other iron studies were not consistent with pure Fe deficiency 
anemia.  Retic index low suggesting inappropriate marrow 
response, consistent with CKD. Pt. received one unit of blood 
with appropriate hemoglobin response.  He also continued EPO at 
hemodialysis.

# ESRD on HD. Anuric. Pt. continued on hemodialysis as well as 
home sevelamer, nephrocaps, cinacalcet, and hydroxyzine. 

# HTN. Pt with slightly elevated BP on arrival.  Given initial 
concern for sepsis and SBO, home isosorbide was initially held, 
but all of his home medications were restarted by the time of 
discharge.

# GERD. Pt. was continued on home omeprazole. 

# Transitional issues:
- Please follow-up pt's calcium. He was hypercalcemic here with 
elevated PTH. Could consider further eval with SPEP/UPEP, PTHrP. 

- Please continue to encourage 1.5L fluid restriction.
- Please monitor O2 sat and volume status. If increased O2 
requirement, he may need additional fluid restriction.
- Consider PFTs for additional evaluation for COPD.
- Pt. will continue with ___ dialysis

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Hypotension.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior exams, most recently of ___.

FINDINGS:

Single frontal view of the chest.  Lung volumes are low, exaggerating heart
size which remains stable.  There is a moderate degree of pulmonary edema with
probable bilateral pleural effusions.  No pneumothorax or lobar consolidation.


IMPRESSION:

Moderate pulmonary edema with probable bilateral pleural effusions.

INDICATION:  Patient with fever to 103 and abdominal pain, evaluate for reason
for abdominal pain such as pancreatitis or abscess.  

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___.  

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was done following
manual intravenous injection of 90cc of Omnipaque through an external jugular
line.  Multiplanar reformatted images in coronal and sagittal axes were
generated.  

DLP:  433 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:

Evaluation of soft tissue and vasculature are somewhat limited due to
suboptimal contrast-enhanced study from manual injection of IV contrast.  

LOWER CHEST:  Ground glass opacities are noted in the bilateral lung bases.  A
small focal consolidation is seen in the right medial lung base.  The heart is
moderately enlarged with coronary artery and aortic valve calcification. 
Previous small pleural effusions have resolved.  

LIVER:  The liver enhances homogeneously without suspicious focal lesions. 
There is no intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation.  The gallbladder is
decompressed and the portal vein is patent.  

PANCREAS: The pancreas enhances homogeneously without evidence of
pancreatitis.  Known hypodense lesions within the pancreatic body are again
demonstrated, largest measuring 10 mm, previously characterized as IPMNs on
MRI from ___.

SPLEEN: The spleen is homogeneous and normal in size.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

KIDNEYS: The kidneys again demonstrate multiple cortical and medullary
hypodensities, suggestive of lithium induced nephropathy.  They enhance
homogeneously and excrete contrast promptly without evidence of
hydronephrosis.  

GI TRACT: Diffusely dilated loops of small bowel measuring up to 4.5cm with
air-fluid levels with gradual decrease in caliber and a relative transition
point seen in the right lower quadrant (2:58).  There is distal decompression
of the remaining small bowel and colon.  There is no evidence of wall
thickening, pneumatosis, or intra-abdominal free air.  The appendix is normal.

VASCULAR: The aorta is of normal caliber without aneurysmal dilatation.  The
IVC and major abdominal vessels are patent.

RETROPERITONEUM AND ABDOMEN: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph
node enlargement.  No ascites or free air is seen.  Note is made of a small
fat containing umbilical hernia.  

PELVIC CT: The urinary bladder and terminal ureters are normal.  No pelvic
wall or inguinal lymph node enlargement is seen.  A penile prosthesis with
pump is in place.  

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: No blastic or lytic lesion suspicious for malignancy is
present.  Diffuse sclerosis compatible with renal osteodystrophy is again
noted.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Dilated loops of small bowel measuring up to 4.5 cm with air-fluid levels
with a relative transition point seen in the right lower quadrant and
decompressed distal bowel.  Findings concerning for small bowel obstruction.  

2.  Focal consolidation is seen in the right mid lung, which may represent
atelectasis or a supervening infection in the appropriate clinical setting. 
Bibasilar ground-glass opacities likely represents edema and/or atelectasis. 
Previous small pleural effusions have resolved.

day of exam.
